old_value: The represented mechanic changes defense, not outgoing TDD.
new_value: Every declared family on this item is a defence: the represented mechanic changes durability, not outgoing TDD.

evidence_tree.built_with: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <scratch>

independent_computation.step_0_leaf_is_prose: This leaf is a coverage-verdict justification string, not a number. The verifiable content is two factual claims: (a) the item's represented mechanic changes the holder's survivability rather than outgoing TDD, and (b) EVERY declared effect family on the item is a defence. (b) is new; it is a universal quantifier that the old string did not assert, so the change is only safe if it holds for the item this coverage entry is about.

step_1_identify_the_scenario.claim: 'syndra_derived_order_120' is a Syndra scenario at the 120-splinter state with a derived cast order.
step_1_identify_the_scenario.quote: "buff (120-splinter +15% total AP capstone)" ... "P = 120-splinter +15% total AP BUFF." ... "splinters option (0-120) gates Q2 second charge, W 60-splinter true-damage (12%+2%/100 AP), P 120-splinter +15% AP buff"
step_1_identify_the_scenario.so: The '120' is the Splinters of Wrath stack option, and Syndra is a mid-lane AP champion. This fixes the role-compatible candidate pool as the mid pool.

step_2_identify_the_item.reasoning: No scenario definitions exist under data/, so the item is identified from the only pinned analogue of this objective in the cached corpus: the mid-role utility BIS coverage scenario.
step_2_identify_the_item.corroboration: data/worklists/e9-bis-b-task.md documents the mechanism producing these strings: "src/calculator/item_coverage.py - how item effects get 'blocked'/'withheld' verdicts and what certification requires" and "convert the withholding into a DOCUMENTED boundary: update the corpus scenario expectation + item coverage note so the withholding is an audited, sourced decision - never silent."
step_2_identify_the_item.conclusion: For a mid-role AP champion under the utility objective, the single non-fully-certified item in the cached pool is Fimbulwinter. That is the item this coverage entry describes. (Banshee's Veil / Verdant Barrier / Zhonya's Hourglass are the only other whole-item-defensive mid candidates; the check below is run against them too, so the verdict does not hinge on the identification.)

step_3_enumerate_the_declared_families_f.universal_claim_result: TRUE. Both — i.e. every — declared effect family on Fimbulwinter is a defence.

step_4_why_the_stat_line_does_not_falsif.quote: health flat 550.0; mana flat 1000.0; abilityHaste flat 15.0
step_4_why_the_stat_line_does_not_falsif.reasoning: Fimbulwinter's 15 ability haste does raise outgoing TDD (docs/math-foundations.md, project domain rule: effective_cd = base_cd x 100/(100 + ability_haste), so more casts land in the window). The coverage reason is therefore necessarily scoped to the item's DECLARED EFFECT FAMILIES (passives[]/active[]), not to its stat block — stats are priced by the stats layer and are never the subject of an effect-coverage verdict. Read at that scope the new string is exactly right, and the same scoping was already implicit in the old string ('the represented mechanic').
step_4_why_the_stat_line_does_not_falsif.cross_check: The same holds for the alternative candidates: Banshee's Veil (3102) grants 105 AP as a stat yet declares exactly one effect family, 'Annul :: Grants a spell shield that blocks the next hostile ability (40 second cooldown...)' — again all-defence.

step_5_terminology.defense_vs_durability: Fimbulwinter grants ZERO armor and ZERO magic resistance (data/items.json 3121 stats: only health, mana, abilityHaste). Its two effects grant bonus health and a shield. 'Defense' colloquially denotes resistances — the quantity R in the engine's mitigation operator (docs/math-foundations.md §1.2: 'the mitigation operator x -> x*100/(100+R)'). 'Durability' is the correct umbrella for health + shields + resistances, i.e. the effective-HP term the engine tiebreaks on (docs/math-foundations.md §3.1: 'with an infinitesimal effective-health tiebreak (score + EHP*1e-9)'). So the new wording is strictly MORE accurate for this item, not merely a paraphrase: the old wording named a quantity the item does not modify.

outgoing_tdd_phrase_is_house_vocabulary.quote: "P (Blast Shield - defensive shield, does not change outgoing TDD)" ... "P Blast Shield is explicitly documented as defensive-only ('does not change outgoing TDD')."
outgoing_tdd_phrase_is_house_vocabulary.note: Confirms 'does not change outgoing TDD' is the established repo phrasing for a defensive-only mechanic; both strings use it consistently.

step_6_falsification_attempt.question: Is there a plausible subject item for which the new universal claim would be FALSE while the old string stayed true?

declared_families: Awe :: Grants ability power equal to 2% bonus mana. (OFFENSIVE)
Manaflow :: bonus mana (resource, not a defence)
Void Infusion :: AP from bonus health (OFFENSIVE)

step_6_falsification_attempt.resolution: None of these can be the subject. The coverage VERDICT itself — the item is excluded from the outgoing-TDD accounting — is only emitted for an item with no outgoing-damage effect family. Any item on that falsifier list declares a family that does move outgoing TDD (Awe->AP, Void Corruption->damage amp, Manaflow->mana feeding an AP/mana scaler), so it would be certified/covered rather than carry this reason. In other words: wherever this reason is legitimately emitted at all, the new universal claim is exactly the condition that licenses it. The strengthening cannot be false while the surrounding verdict is true.

independent_computation.step_7_conclusion: For the subject item (Fimbulwinter under the mid-role utility objective; and equally for every other item that can legitimately carry this verdict), both claims in the new string hold: (a) every declared effect family is a defence — bonus health and a shield, with no damage atom emitted from either fragment; (b) the represented mechanic changes durability, not outgoing TDD. The old string is not false but is (i) under-justified — it speaks of a single 'represented mechanic' for an item that declares two effect families, and (ii) imprecise — it says 'defense' for an item that grants no armor or magic resistance, only health and a shield. The new string fixes both.
